entries.test: Public comparative studies of unintentional wholesale fabrication by humans and LLMs, excluding the specified disorder-associated hallucinations, would test the claimed difference.
entries.note: Context distinguishes unintentional fabrication from lying, jokes, and flawed arguments.

entries.test: Published research on LLM hallucination mechanisms and human memory failures would establish whether their mechanisms and characteristic errors differ as claimed.
entries.note: This compares mechanisms; it does not assert that one phenomenon causes the other.

entries.test: Published training-data extraction experiments and the research literature available by February 2024 would establish both memorization and a research subfield devoted to it.

entries.note: Whether Hinton acknowledged the literature is factual; looking seriously out of touch is an evaluative judgment.
Marcus expresses doubt and a conceivable attribution, rather than a firm conclusion that deep understanding is absent.

entries.test: Public controlled evaluations of contemporary LLM reasoning, reliability, hallucination, and fact-checking, including interventions on their reasoning capabilities, would test the asserted limitations and causal explanation.
entries.note: Marcus explicitly endorses his own quoted words. The surrounding discussion connects understanding to common sense and causal reasoning.
The overall claim evaluates Hinton's argument and manner, rather than being empty rhetoric. Its embedded assertion about classical AI experts could be checked separately.

entries.test: Public OpenAI disclosures or documented filtering changes and contemporaneous replication tests would establish whether OpenAI had blocked this specific example by February 5, 2024.
entries.note: “Will no doubt by now have” expresses firm confidence about an already completed action, not a future deadline.
